a: Supper was under way
p: The KJV says "supper being ended," from a later reading. The older text says supper was going on.

readings.w: Sinaiticus (first hand) and Vaticanus (300s), Codex Regius (L) and Washington (W), as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: δείπνου γινομένου
readings.en: while supper was taking place
readings.plain: Supper was under way

readings.w: Papyrus 66 (about 200), Alexandrinus and Bezae (400s), Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV "supper being ended")
readings.orig: δείπνου γενομένου
readings.en: when supper had come (or: had ended)
readings.plain: Supper was over

why: The present participle has early and strong support and fits the story, since the meal is still going on in 13:26. The aorist can mean "when supper had come," but the KJV took it as "ended," which clashes with 13:12 and 13:26.

a: planted the plan in the heart that Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, would hand Jesus over
p: In the older text, the devil puts the plan into "the heart," and Judas is named as the one who will act. In the KJV, the devil puts it "into the heart of Judas."

readings.w: NA28, SBLGNT, Westcott-Hort
readings.orig: τοῦ διαβόλου ἤδη βεβληκότος εἰς τὴν καρδίαν ἵνα παραδοῖ αὐτὸν Ἰούδας Σίμωνος Ἰσκαριώτου
readings.en: the devil having already put into the heart that Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, would hand him over
readings.plain: planted the plan in the heart that Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, would hand Jesus over

readings.w: Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV "into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon's son, to betray him")
readings.orig: τοῦ διαβόλου ἤδη βεβληκότος εἰς τὴν καρδίαν Ἰούδα Σίμωνος Ἰσκαριώτου ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδῷ
readings.en: the devil having already put into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, to hand him over
readings.plain: planted it in the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, to hand Jesus over

why: The older wording is awkward, since it does not say whose heart. Some scholars think it means the devil's own heart: the devil had made up his mind. Copyists made it smooth by putting Judas's name with "heart." The awkward reading is more likely the original.
b: The Tyndale House edition has the same order as NA28 but spells the last name Ἰσκαριώτης, so that "Iscariot" belongs to Judas, not to Simon. The meaning of the story is the same either way: Judas acts, and the devil is behind it.

a: has no need to wash, except the feet
p: Codex Sinaiticus and some Latin witnesses leave out "except the feet," which changes the meaning of the bath.

readings.w: Papyrus 66, Vaticanus and nearly all other manuscripts, as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT; Byzantine (with a slightly different wording, ἢ τοὺς πόδας)
readings.orig: οὐκ ἔχει χρείαν εἰ μὴ τοὺς πόδας νίψασθαι
readings.en: has no need except to wash the feet
readings.plain: has no need to wash, except the feet

readings.w: Codex Sinaiticus (300s), some Old Latin manuscripts and Origen, as reported by Metzger
readings.orig: οὐκ ἔχει χρείαν νίψασθαι
readings.en: has no need to wash
readings.plain: has no need to wash

why: The longer reading is in nearly all manuscripts, according to Metzger. The shorter reading is attractive to some scholars (Bultmann, Barrett, Lincoln), because then the "bath" is the foot washing itself, and Jesus's point is that his washing makes them completely clean; they argue that copyists added "except the feet" to fit a church practice. Most editors keep the words because the evidence for them is so broad.
b: If the short text is original, the foot washing stands for the whole cleansing Jesus gives in his death. With the long text, a distinction is made between a once-for-all bath and a repeated washing of the feet, which many readers apply to baptism and later forgiveness.

a: The one who eats my bread
p: The KJV reads "He that eateth bread with me," following most manuscripts. The critical text has "my bread."

readings.w: Vaticanus, Ephraemi Rescriptus and Regius (L), as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: ὁ τρώγων μου τὸν ἄρτον
readings.en: the one who eats my bread
readings.plain: The one who eats my bread

readings.w: Papyrus 66, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Bezae, Washington, Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV)
readings.orig: ὁ τρώγων μετ' ἐμοῦ τὸν ἄρτον
readings.en: the one who eats bread with me
readings.plain: The one who eats bread with me

why: "My bread" matches the Hebrew of Psalm 41:9 ("who ate my bread"), and a copyist was more likely to change it to the familiar Gospel phrase "with me" (Mark 14:18) than the reverse. The witnesses for "with me" are older and more numerous, so the decision is close.

a: gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot
p: Editions differ on whether Jesus "took" the bite before giving it, and on how Judas's name is given.

readings.w: SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: βάψας οὖν τὸ ψωμίον δίδωσιν Ἰούδᾳ Σίμωνος Ἰσκαριώτου
readings.en: so having dipped the bite he gives it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot
readings.plain: gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot

readings.w: NA28, Westcott-Hort, Tregelles
readings.orig: βάψας οὖν τὸ ψωμίον λαμβάνει καὶ δίδωσιν Ἰούδᾳ Σίμωνος Ἰσκαριώτου
readings.en: so having dipped the bite he takes it and gives it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot
readings.plain: took it and gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot

readings.w: Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine text, Textus Receptus (KJV "he gave it to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon")
readings.orig: καὶ ἐμβάψας τὸ ψωμίον δίδωσιν Ἰούδᾳ Σίμωνος Ἰσκαριώτῃ
readings.en: and having dipped the bite he gives it to Judas Iscariot, son of Simon
readings.plain: gave it to Judas Iscariot, son of Simon

why: NA28 prints "takes and" in brackets as uncertain; the other modern editions leave it out. The words could be added to echo the Lord's Supper ("he took bread"). Either way, nothing in the story changes.

a: And if God has been glorified in him, God himself
p: Many of the oldest manuscripts lack "If God has been glorified in him." The Tyndale House edition leaves it out.

readings.w: Sinaiticus (corrected), Alexandrinus, Ephraemi (corrected), Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV); NA28 (in brackets), SBLGNT
readings.orig: εἰ ὁ θεὸς ἐδοξάσθη ἐν αὐτῷ, καὶ ὁ θεὸς δοξάσει αὐτόν
readings.en: if God has been glorified in him, God also will glorify him
readings.plain: And if God has been glorified in him, God himself

readings.w: Papyrus 66, Sinaiticus (first hand), Vaticanus, Ephraemi (first hand), Bezae, Washington and others, as reported by Metzger; Tyndale House GNT, Westcott and Hort
readings.orig: καὶ ὁ θεὸς δοξάσει αὐτόν
readings.en: and God will glorify him
readings.plain: God himself

why: The clause repeats the end of 13:31, and a copyist's eye could easily skip from one "in him" to the next, which would explain its loss even in early manuscripts. The NA28 committee kept it in brackets for that reason. The Tyndale House editors judged the early omission decisive. The meaning changes little.

a: Otherwise, would I have said to you that I am on my way to get a place ready for you?
p: The oldest manuscripts have a small word (hoti) that turns the sentence into a question. The KJV has a statement.

readings.w: Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus, Bezae and others; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: εἰ δὲ μή, εἶπον ἂν ὑμῖν ὅτι πορεύομαι ἑτοιμάσαι τόπον ὑμῖν;
readings.en: otherwise, would I have told you that I go to prepare a place for you?
readings.plain: Otherwise, would I have said to you that I am on my way to get a place ready for you?

readings.w: Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV "if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you")
readings.orig: εἰ δὲ μή, εἶπον ἂν ὑμῖν· πορεύομαι ἑτοιμάσαι τόπον ὑμῖν
readings.en: otherwise, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you
readings.plain: Otherwise, I would have said so to you. I am on my way to get a place ready for you.

why: "Hoti" has the best early support and is the harder reading: Jesus has not said before that he goes to prepare a place, so copyists probably dropped the word to smooth the sense. With it, the sentence can be a question (as in the Plain) or can mean "I would have told you, because I go..."

a: And you know the way that leads where I am going.
p: The KJV doubles the verb: "whither I go ye know, and the way ye know."

readings.w: Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Ephraemi (first hand), Regius (L), Washington, as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: καὶ ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω οἴδατε τὴν ὁδόν
readings.en: and where I am going you know the way
readings.plain: And you know the way that leads where I am going.

readings.w: Alexandrinus, Bezae, Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV)
readings.orig: καὶ ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω οἴδατε καὶ τὴν ὁδὸν οἴδατε
readings.en: and where I am going you know, and the way you know
readings.plain: And you know where I am going, and you know the way.

why: The short form is awkward Greek, and copyists likely smoothed it by adding "you know, and" to prepare for Thomas's two-part reply in 14:5.

a: If you knew me, you would know my Father too.
p: The manuscripts differ: "If you had known me, you would have known my Father" or "If you know me, you will know my Father."

readings.w: Vaticanus, Ephraemi (first hand) and others with ᾔδειτε ἄν; Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority with ἐγνώκειτε ἄν (same sense; Textus Receptus, KJV); SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: εἰ ἐγνώκειτέ με, καὶ τὸν πατέρα μου ἂν ᾔδειτε
readings.en: if you had known me, you would have known my Father also
readings.plain: If you knew me, you would know my Father too.

readings.w: Papyrus 66, Sinaiticus and Bezae (first hand), as reported by Metzger; NA28
readings.orig: εἰ ἐγνώκατέ με, καὶ τὸν πατέρα μου γνώσεσθε
readings.en: if you have come to know me, you will know my Father too
readings.plain: If you have come to know me, you will know my Father too.

why: This is a place where the editions part ways. The NA28 committee preferred the promise, found in the earliest papyrus and Sinaiticus, thinking copyists turned it into a rebuke like 8:19. The SBLGNT and the Tyndale House editors preferred the rebuke, supported by Vaticanus and most manuscripts, which fits Jesus's mild reproach to Philip in 14:9. The Plain follows the SBLGNT. The next sentence, "Starting now you know him," makes sense with either.

a: ask me for anything
p: The critical editions read "ask me." The KJV, and some manuscripts, leave out "me"; a few leave out the whole verse.

readings.w: Papyrus 66, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Washington and others, as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT; Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine text
readings.orig: ἐάν τι αἰτήσητέ με ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου
readings.en: if you ask me anything in my name
readings.plain: ask me for anything

readings.w: Alexandrinus, Bezae, Regius (L), many later manuscripts, Textus Receptus (KJV)
readings.orig: ἐάν τι αἰτήσητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου
readings.en: if you ask anything in my name
readings.plain: ask for anything

why: "Me" has the stronger early support. Copyists probably dropped it because it seemed odd to pray to Jesus "in Jesus's name," and because 15:16 and 16:23 speak of asking the Father.
b: A few witnesses (among them some Old Latin manuscripts and the Sinaitic Syriac) omit the whole verse, perhaps because it repeats 14:13. The verse with "me" is one of the clearest places in the Gospels where prayer is addressed to Jesus himself.

a: you will keep the commands I give
p: Is this a promise ("you will keep") or a command ("keep")? The KJV has the command.

readings.w: Vaticanus, Regius (L), Psi, as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: ἐὰν ἀγαπᾶτέ με, τὰς ἐντολὰς τὰς ἐμὰς τηρήσετε
readings.en: if you love me, you will keep my commands
readings.plain: you will keep the commands I give

readings.w: Alexandrinus, Bezae, Washington, Theta, family 13, Byzantine majority, as reported by Metzger; Textus Receptus (KJV "keep my commandments")
readings.orig: τὰς ἐντολὰς τὰς ἐμὰς τηρήσατε
readings.en: keep my commands
readings.plain: keep the commands I give

readings.w: Papyrus 66, Sinaiticus, as reported by Metzger
readings.orig: τὰς ἐντολὰς τὰς ἐμὰς τηρήσητε
readings.en: (if) you keep my commands
readings.plain: and if you keep the commands I give,

why: The Greek forms differ by one or two letters, so copyists easily mixed them up. The future fits the pattern of 14:21, 23, where love and keeping go together. The third form joins the line to 14:16: "if you love me and keep my commands, I will ask the Father."
b: With the future, obedience is the fruit of love, not a condition laid on top of it. With the command, it is an instruction. Both ideas are found elsewhere in John (15:10, 14).

a: he will be in you
p: Some early manuscripts read "he is in you," making the Spirit's indwelling already present.

readings.w: Papyrus 66 (corrected), Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV); NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσται
readings.en: will be in you
readings.plain: he will be in you

readings.w: Papyrus 66 (first hand), Vaticanus, Bezae (first hand), Washington, as reported by Metzger; Westcott and Hort
readings.orig: ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστιν
readings.en: is in you
readings.plain: he is in you

why: The future fits the promise of the Spirit to come (14:16, 26; 16:7). The present may have come from the present "remains" just before. The evidence is divided, and some scholars prefer the present as the harder reading.

a: the Father is greater
p: The KJV reads "I go unto the Father: for my Father is greater than I" and also adds "I said" earlier in the verse.

readings.w: NA28, SBLGNT
readings.orig: ὁ πατὴρ μείζων μού ἐστιν
readings.en: the Father is greater than I
readings.plain: the Father is greater

readings.w: Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV); Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: ὁ πατήρ μου μείζων μού ἐστιν
readings.en: my Father is greater than I
readings.plain: my Father is greater

why: The Plain follows the NA28 and SBLGNT. The Tyndale House edition prints "my Father" here. The difference does not change the theological question discussed in the note on this verse.
b: The Byzantine text also reads "because I said, 'I am going to the Father'" (εἶπον, πορεύομαι), which the KJV follows ("because I said, I go unto the Father"). The meaning is the same.

a: ask for anything you want
p: The older text says "ask" (a command). The Byzantine text and KJV say "ye shall ask."

readings.w: NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT; Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine text
readings.orig: ὃ ἐὰν θέλητε αἰτήσασθε
readings.en: ask whatever you want
readings.plain: ask for anything you want

readings.w: Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV "ye shall ask what ye will")
readings.orig: ὃ ἐὰν θέλητε αἰτήσεσθε
readings.en: you will ask whatever you want
readings.plain: you will ask for anything you want

why: The two forms differ by one vowel in Greek and sounded alike when read aloud. The imperative has the better early support.

a: and become disciples of mine
p: Some manuscripts read a future, "and so you will be my disciples" (KJV).

readings.w: Vaticanus, Bezae, Regius (L) and others, as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: καὶ γένησθε ἐμοὶ μαθηταί
readings.en: and become my disciples
readings.plain: and become disciples of mine

readings.w: Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV "so shall ye be my disciples")
readings.orig: καὶ γενήσεσθε ἐμοὶ μαθηταί
readings.en: and you will be my disciples
readings.plain: and so you will become disciples of mine

why: The evidence is evenly balanced and the forms sound alike. With the subjunctive, bearing fruit and becoming disciples are one thing that glorifies the Father; with the future, discipleship is the result of bearing fruit. The editors chose the subjunctive with some hesitation.

a: you will have my joy in you
p: The KJV reads "that my joy might remain in you."

readings.w: NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ἡ ἐμὴ ἐν ὑμῖν ᾖ
readings.en: that my joy may be in you
readings.plain: you will have my joy in you

readings.w: Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV)
readings.orig: ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ἡ ἐμὴ ἐν ὑμῖν μείνῃ
readings.en: that my joy may remain in you
readings.plain: my joy will remain in you

why: "Remain" looks like a copyist's echo of the many "remain" words in 15:4–10. The plainer "be" has the older support.

a: their hour
p: The critical text says "their hour," the time of the persecutors. The Byzantine text and KJV have "the time."

readings.w: NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἡ ὥρα αὐτῶν
readings.en: when their hour comes
readings.plain: their hour

readings.w: Some early manuscripts, Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV "when the time shall come")
readings.orig: ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἡ ὥρα
readings.en: when the hour comes
readings.plain: the hour

why: "Their hour" is the more unusual phrase, setting the persecutors' hour against Jesus's own "hour"; copyists may have dropped "their" as unclear or have been influenced by 16:2, 25.

a: lead you in all the truth
p: Older manuscripts are divided between "in all the truth" and "into all the truth" (KJV).

readings.w: Sinaiticus, Bezae, Regius (L), Washington, as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT
readings.orig: ὁδηγήσει ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πάσῃ
readings.en: will guide you in all the truth
readings.plain: lead you in all the truth

readings.w: Alexandrinus, Vaticanus; Tyndale House GNT, Westcott and Hort (εἰς τὴν ἀλήθειαν πᾶσαν); Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV) (εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν)
readings.orig: ὁδηγήσει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν ἀλήθειαν πᾶσαν
readings.en: will guide you into all the truth
readings.plain: lead you into all the truth

why: The NA28 and SBLGNT follow "in," judging that copyists changed it to the usual construction "guide into." The Tyndale House edition prefers "into" with Vaticanus. "Into" suggests a journey toward truth not yet reached; "in" suggests guidance within the whole truth already given in Jesus.

a: Then a short time again, and you will see me.
p: The KJV adds "because I go to the Father" at the end of the verse, from 16:17.

readings.w: Papyrus 5 and Papyrus 66 (about 200–300), Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae, Regius (L), Washington; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν καὶ ὄψεσθέ με
readings.en: and again a little while and you will see me
readings.plain: Then a short time again, and you will see me.

readings.w: Alexandrinus, Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV)
readings.orig: καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν καὶ ὄψεσθέ με, ὅτι ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πατέρα
readings.en: and again a little while and you will see me, because I go to the Father
readings.plain: Then a short time again, and you will see me, because I am going to the Father.

why: The addition is missing from the earliest witnesses and is easily explained: in 16:17 the disciples quote Jesus as saying "because I am going to the Father" (from 16:10), so copyists supplied the words here.

a: if you ask the Father for anything, he will give it to you in my name
p: In the older text, "in my name" goes with the Father's giving. In the Byzantine text and KJV it goes with the asking.

readings.w: Papyrus 5, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Ephraemi (first hand), Regius (L), as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: ἄν τι αἰτήσητε τὸν πατέρα δώσει ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου
readings.en: whatever you ask the Father, he will give you in my name
readings.plain: if you ask the Father for anything, he will give it to you in my name

readings.w: Alexandrinus, Bezae, Washington, Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV "whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you")
readings.orig: ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσητε τὸν πατέρα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου δώσει ὑμῖν
readings.en: whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you
readings.plain: whatever you ask the Father for in my name, he will give it to you

why: The older order is unusual, and copyists probably moved "in my name" to match 14:13; 15:16 and 16:24. With the older order, the Father's gifts come to the disciples through Jesus.

a: came out from God
p: A few strong manuscripts read "from the Father," which Westcott and Hort printed.

readings.w: Papyrus 5, Sinaiticus (first hand), Alexandrinus, Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV); NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐξῆλθον
readings.en: I came from God
readings.plain: came out from God

readings.w: Vaticanus, Ephraemi (first hand), Bezae, Regius (L), as reported by Metzger; Westcott and Hort
readings.orig: παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐξῆλθον
readings.en: I came from the Father
readings.plain: came out from the Father

why: "The Father" could have come in from the next verse, "I came out from the Father." The meaning is the same.

a: In the world you have hardship
p: The KJV reads "ye shall have tribulation," a future. The other editions have a present.

readings.w: NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT; Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine text
readings.orig: ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ θλῖψιν ἔχετε
readings.en: in the world you have hardship
readings.plain: In the world you have hardship

readings.w: Textus Receptus (KJV "ye shall have tribulation")
readings.orig: ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ θλῖψιν ἕξετε
readings.en: in the world you will have hardship
readings.plain: In the world you will have hardship

why: The present has the support of both the critical editions and the Byzantine text. With the present, hardship is already part of the disciples' life, not only a future danger.

a: them safe in your name, the name you have given me
t: The name, or the people, that the Father gave
p: In the critical text the Father gave Jesus his name. The KJV reads "those whom thou hast given me."

readings.w: Nearly all Greek manuscripts, including Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: τήρησον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ᾧ δέδωκάς μοι
readings.en: keep them in your name, which you have given me
readings.plain: them safe in your name, the name you have given me

readings.w: A few manuscripts; Textus Receptus (KJV)
readings.orig: τήρησον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου οὓς δέδωκάς μοι
readings.en: keep through your name those whom you have given me
readings.plain: safe in your name those you have given me

why: The idea that the Father gave his name to the Son is unusual, so scribes changed "which" (the name) to "whom" (the disciples), matching 17:6, 9. The reading with "which" is far better supported.
b: If the Father has given the Son his own name, the claim is very high: in Jewish tradition God's name was his alone (Isaiah 42:8). Compare Philippians 2:9 and Revelation 19:12–13.

a: When I was with them, I kept them safe in your name, the name you have given me
t: "In the world," and the name again
p: The Byzantine text adds "in the world" and, like the KJV, reads "those that thou gavest me."

readings.w: Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and other early manuscripts, as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: ὅτε ἤμην μετ' αὐτῶν ἐγὼ ἐτήρουν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ᾧ δέδωκάς μοι
readings.en: when I was with them, I kept them in your name, which you have given me
readings.plain: When I was with them, I kept them safe in your name, the name you have given me

readings.w: Alexandrinus, Ephraemi (corrected), Bezae, Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV)
readings.orig: ὅτε ἤμην μετ' αὐτῶν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, ἐγὼ ἐτήρουν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου· οὓς δέδωκάς μοι ἐφύλαξα
readings.en: when I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name; those whom you gave me I guarded
readings.plain: When I was with them in the world, I kept safe in your name those you have given me

why: As in 17:11, "which" (the name) is the harder and better supported reading. "In the world" was probably added from 17:11, 13.

a: in the truth
p: Later manuscripts and the KJV read "through thy truth."

readings.w: NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT; Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine text
readings.orig: ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ
readings.en: in the truth
readings.plain: in the truth

readings.w: Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV "through thy truth")
readings.orig: ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ σου

why: "Your" was probably added to match "your word" in the next clause. The sense is the same.

a: let them also be in us
p: Many manuscripts, the Tyndale House edition and the KJV read "that they also may be one in us."

readings.w: Vaticanus, Ephraemi (first hand), Bezae and Old Latin manuscripts, as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT
readings.orig: ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἡμῖν ὦσιν
readings.en: that they also may be in us
readings.plain: let them also be in us

readings.w: Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Ephraemi (corrected), Regius (L), Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV); Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἡμῖν ἓν ὦσιν
readings.en: that they also may be one in us
readings.plain: let them also be one in us

why: "One" could easily be added from the start of the verse and from 17:11, 22, so the shorter text is preferred by NA28 and SBLGNT. The Tyndale House editors judged the longer reading original, since "one" could also have been lost by accident. The meaning hardly changes.

a: what you have given me, I want them to be with me where I am
p: The oldest manuscripts use a neuter "what" for the disciples. Later ones, and the KJV, smooth it to "those whom."

readings.w: Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae, Washington and others, as reported by Metzger; NA28, SBLGNT, Tyndale House GNT
readings.orig: ὃ δέδωκάς μοι, θέλω ἵνα ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ κἀκεῖνοι ὦσιν μετ' ἐμοῦ
readings.en: what you have given me, I want that where I am they also may be with me
readings.plain: what you have given me, I want them to be with me where I am

readings.w: Alexandrinus, Ephraemi, Regius (L), Byzantine majority, Textus Receptus (KJV)
readings.orig: οὓς δέδωκάς μοι, θέλω ἵνα ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ κἀκεῖνοι ὦσιν μετ' ἐμοῦ
readings.en: those whom you have given me, I want that where I am they also may be with me
readings.plain: I want those you have given me to be with me where I am

why: The neuter is the harder reading and matches John's style in 6:37, 39 and 17:2, where the disciples as a whole are "all that" the Father gave. Scribes corrected it to the plural.
